title: ROS2 & Gazebo Robotics Simulation
summary: Simulated a custom robot in ROS2 and Gazebo with sensor integration, control, and navigation — intermediate proficiency reached in under 3 weeks.
description: Designed and simulated a custom robot in ROS2 and Gazebo, utilizing the publish-subscribe model for sensor integration, control, and navigation. I pursued this project after my senior year (graduated high school) as a continuation of my ISM dog robot project seen in the project tile below. I wanted to run simulations of my dog robot with an industry-certified tool like ROS2. In just under 3 weeks I accomplished an intermediate level of proficiency in the ROS2 framework, and its methods of communication with simulators like RViz and Gazebo through Udemy certifications. Future Plans: During my freshman year as an ECE Honors major at UT Austin, I plan to implement the 3D .stl model of my robot design into Gazebo and start programming its limbs and test its movement virtually before running the ROS2 framework on the real bot.

title: Bio-Inspired Robotics Research — Energy Efficiency
role: Independent Researcher, ISM Program @ Liberty HS
summary: Year-long ISM research initiative prototyping three bio-inspired robots for hazardous environments — custom PCBs, soft robotics, and Fusion 360 CAD.
description: Prototyped three bio-inspired robots to explore optimal locomotion and energy efficiency. Led a year-long ISM research initiative focused on robotics for hazardous environments like space and underwater missions. Designed soft robotic systems inspired by octopus suction and spider-like movement, engineered custom PCBs, programmed embedded systems in Python and C++, and simulated performance using ROS. CAD models were created in Fusion 360 and fabricated with an Ender 3 printer, and finally presented at the ISM End-of-Year Showcase with the entire school district.

title: FRC Robotics - Team 7503 Radicubs
summary: Led a 30+ member robotics team through full-cycle robot development, autonomous navigation, and over $20K in sponsorships.
description: Led a 30+ member robotics team through full-cycle robot development for FIRST Robotics Competition, oversaw and thoroughly led CAD prototyping in Fusion 360 for two straight seasons, autonomous navigation using AprilTags on Jetson Nano, and pneumatics-based climbing mechanisms. Programmed pathfinding modules, optimized shooter kinematics, and engineered button-board layouts. Managed team logistics, secured $20K+ in sponsorships, and mentored FRC/FLL teams.

title: Alertify - Public Safety App
summary: Developed a Swift-based mobile app to alert school security systems during life-threatening scenarios, integrating Firebase and Twilio APIs.
description: Designed and built Alertify, a mobile app for emergency alerts in school environments. Conducted user research, built frontend in Swift/Xcode, and implemented backend with Firebase and Twilio APIs for real-time messaging. Recognized by Congressman Pat Fallon for innovation in public safety.

title: Emotion Detection for Autism Support
summary: Built a CNN-based emotion detection model using OpenCV to support children with autism, as part of Inspirit AI research.
description: Collaborated on an emotion detection model using CNNs and OpenCV to help children with autism. Explored reinforcement learning for robotic control tasks like pendulum balancing. Mentored by researchers from Brown and Harvard, and earned DeepLearning.AI certification.

title: DIY Hand Crank Generator
summary: After learning about electromagnetic induction from Physics 2, tested the theory with a hand crank generator built from 3D-printed gears and coils, generating 1V of potential difference.
description: After learning about electromagnetic induction from my Physics 2 class, I went on to test the theory with my own hand crank generator. I modeled and 3D-printed two beveled gears, with the big gear having six magnets attached while three coils were stationary and in series to induce current. I was able to generate 1 V of potential difference.

title: DIY Air Quality Monitoring System
summary: Engineered a low-cost air and water quality monitoring system using Raspberry Pi and custom sensors, logging real-time data for analysis.
description: Built a Raspberry Pi-based system to monitor air and water quality using PM2.5/PM10 sensors and a DIY turbidity sensor. Displayed data on an LCD and logged to CSV files. Simulated unhealthy conditions to test accuracy. Earned second place and a $250 award.

title: Active Speaker Detection Research @ UTD
role: Research Intern, UT Dallas CVMC Lab
summary: Researched and developed models for detecting active speakers in multimodal scenarios using computer vision and audio analysis.
description: Interned at UT Dallas CVMC Lab under Prof. Yapeng Tian. Led research on Active Speaker Detection using computer vision and audio streams. Developed Deep Q-learning models and presented findings to faculty. Drafting manuscript for Journal of Student Research.

title: AI Facial Emotion based Therapy Bot
summary: Built a mental health chatbot using facial emotion recognition and OpenAI LLMs, placing 4th out of 107 submissions.
description: Developed a therapy chatbot that uses YOLO and OpenCV for live emotion detection and OpenAI LLMs for generating therapist-like responses. Placed 4th out of 107 entries at UTD's AI For All Hackathon in 2023.
